CRM.rationale: Salesforce presents a solid fundamental case with improving profitability and strong competitive positioning, partially offset by AI disruption concerns and a mixed near-term catalyst picture. The company shows strong sequential revenue growth (+4.1% QoQ to $10.24B in Q2 FY2026) and accelerating EPS (+23.3% QoQ to $1.96), with gross margins of 78% and operating margins expanding to 22.8%. The balance sheet is healthy with $61.3B equity, low debt-to-equity of 0.14, and manageable leverage. Valuation has compressed significantly: P/E of 39x sits near the bottom of its 34.6-61.1x range over the past year, and P/B of 3.07x is at the low end of 2.7-4.8x, representing a meaningful discount to recent history. The company holds ~20.7% global CRM market share (#1 for 12 consecutive years) and serves 150,000+ customers including 90% of Fortune 500. However, headwinds include AI disruption fears pressuring the per-seat licensing model, FY2027 revenue guidance perceived as lukewarm, and operating cash flow volatility ($740M in Q2 vs $6.48B in Q1). The $50B buyback authorization and $25B accelerated share repurchase signal management confidence, but stock-based compensation dilution partially offsets this. Near-term catalyst: Q1 FY2027 earnings on May 27, 2026, with consensus expecting EPS of $3.12 (+20.9% YoY) and revenue of $11.06B (+12.5% YoY), which could re-rate the stock if execution meets or beats expectations. News sentiment is mixed (mean -0.01) with recent positive coverage of AI integration partnerships and analyst buy recommendations, balanced against AI disruption concerns.
